To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The perturbative multi-Higgs cross-sections at high multiplicities grow exponentially with the multiplicity and violate perturbative Unitarity.

the perturbative multi-Higgs production cross-sections at high multiplicities grow exponentially with the number of Higgs bosons produced and violate perturbative-unitarity at surprisingly low energies ∼ 40−50 TeV with ∼ 150 Higgs bosons in the final states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of multi-Higgs final states in scalar QFT.
the study of the scattering amplitudes of multi-Higgs production in the high multiplicity regime, and the computation of the corresponding total cross-sections.
a study of the perturbative multi-Higgs production at very high energies in the simplest possible scalar field theory models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Higgs boson is the most fundamental particle discovered so far, but the Standard Model of Particle Physics (SM) is not the ultimate theory of Nature.

the Higgs boson has been discovered and its properties measured to a high level of precision, and the Higgs bosons have been observed to decay into pairs of fermions, pairs of bosons, and into a single boson and a single fermion.
the perturbative unitary bound on the cross-sections is not a fundamental limit of the theory but rather a signal of the onset of a non-perturbatively coupled regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high-energy behavior of multi-Higgs scattering processes is very similar to that of multi-gluon processes, with the exception that the former is not as strongly coupled.
we have computed the multi-Higgs processes with up to 5 Higgs particles in the final states and up to 7 final state particles in general, using the MadGraph.

we have computed the total cross-sections for multi-particle final state processes in the high multiplicity regime with MadGraph, and have determined the scaling properties of the cross-sections with the number of produced particles, and the energy scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multi-particle amplitudes grow factorially with n, but the total cross-sections grow only polynomially with n.

the growth in cross-sections at very high energies can be computed with the help of a few diagrams, and that this growth is universal for a wide class of theories, including those with spontaneously broken symmetries.

the multi-Higgs processes in the high-multiplicities regime are very sensitive to the underlying theory, which can be probed by measuring the multi-Higgs production rates at the LHC and the future colliders.
